buttonLabel: "Learn more about wildlife watching on this three-country route"
lead: >-
  For wildlife watching on a journey through Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay, the key part of the current itinerary is in the Galápagos. In Ecuador, the program includes watching giant tortoises on Santa Cruz and one of two boat excursions to nearby islands. Chile is represented by Santiago and a crossing through the Atacama region, while Uruguay features a city tour of Montevideo. Here we explain what the nature-focused section includes, which wildlife encounters are possible and how to plan the short island stay.
---

## Where you can actually watch wildlife on this combination

Our selection for these countries and this interest includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The [32-day grand tour of eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits Uruguay, Chile and Ecuador as part of a longer itinerary that also includes Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Colombia. This is **not a dedicated wildlife tour of the three countries**.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

“Safaris and Wildlife Watching” is a secondary theme of the overall trip; its main themes are culture and nature. The experiences are unevenly distributed among the three countries: **purposeful wildlife watching is confirmed primarily in the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/)**. Uruguay features a historical city tour, while Chile offers a sightseeing visit to Santiago and a drive into the arid high-altitude region, without a separately scheduled wildlife-watching excursion.

It would therefore be misleading to compare this itinerary with a specialist safari covering Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay equally. It suits travelers who want to experience Galápagos wildlife as part of a broad introduction to the continent.

## Santa Cruz: giant tortoises and lava tunnels

After flying from Quito, the group lands on Baltra, crosses the Itabaca Channel and heads to [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). On the way to Puerto Ayora, there is an excursion to the [Santa Cruz Highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/). The description of this excursion lists giant land tortoises in their natural habitat, Darwin's finches and a walk through lava tunnels.

This is where the wildlife portion begins to differ from the city visits: travelers observe living animals in their own habitat rather than viewing them in an exhibition or zoo. Moving quietly along permitted paths and following the local guide's instructions are important. Seeing an animal at close range does not mean that you may touch or feed it, or leave the trail.

Santa Cruz is scheduled **for the day of arrival in the islands**, after several modes of transport. It is better to allow for travel fatigue rather than plan additional independent outings that evening.

## The second island day: North Seymour or South Plaza

The next day includes a boat excursion. The itinerary provides **two alternative options, of which one is confirmed**:

- [North Seymour and Bachas Beach](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/): landing on a rocky shore and walking among birds, including frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies; then a beach and lagoon, with swimming or snorkeling possible subject to the itinerary's conditions.
- [South Plaza Island](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/) with Carrion Point: a sea crossing and a walk near colonies of sea lions, land iguanas and seabirds.

A single day cannot be presented as a guaranteed visit to Seymour, Bachas, Plaza and Carrion together. The confirmed boat excursion, island visiting conditions and weather may influence which option is chosen. Each standalone excursion has its own service details; its individual booking terms should not automatically be applied to the price of the longer tour.

Wildlife sightings depend on nature. The descriptions name species associated with these excursions, but **an encounter with any particular bird, tortoise or sea lion is not guaranteed**. Keep a respectful distance, listen to the guide and allow for changes to landing arrangements. If seeing a specific species is your priority, mention it before finalizing the itinerary.

## What Chile and Uruguay add to this itinerary

[Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) features a city sightseeing tour, while [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) is a stop before the high-altitude route into Bolivia. Desert landscapes and the transition from city to arid terrain add a natural contrast to the journey, but the itinerary here **does not include a separate guaranteed desert wildlife-watching tour**.

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited on a day trip from Buenos Aires. The plan includes a ferry crossing, visits to the port, Independence Square and the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), followed by a return to Argentina. This is a cultural stop, without a scheduled birdwatching outing or nature park visit.

These differences matter when choosing a tour: each of the three countries serves a different purpose in the full itinerary. If animals and volcanic islands are your main goal, compare [wildlife-watching tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) and the time they actually spend in the Galápagos. If you want both cities and island fauna, the longer itinerary offers that contrast.

## Preparing for the wildlife section without unrealistic promises

The island section involves a bus, ferry crossing, car and boat. Comfortable closed-toe shoes, a hat, sun protection and belongings that can be quickly protected from spray are useful for the walks. Check landing conditions and whether you can take part in snorkeling separately: swimming with a mask is not the same as a compulsory scuba dive.

The complete trip has a demanding sequence of transfers. The group returns from Uruguay to Argentina and then flies to Chile; Ecuador comes after Bolivia and Peru. There are high-altitude days in between, so health, altitude adjustment and flight fatigue should be considered for the whole journey, even though the Galápagos themselves are at sea level.

Ada Tours helps select the sequence of stops and coordinate the island excursion day according to the availability of the chosen option, tickets and transfers. During planning, current entry requirements, island permits and fees are checked for each traveler's citizenship and specific dates. A thematic label is not a basis for stating a fixed fee or guaranteeing admission.

Compare the destinations in the [general Chile, Ecuador and Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/chile_ecuador_uruguay/), or browse other itineraries with planned wildlife encounters in the [multi-country wildlife tours selection](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/). For deserts and other scenic routes, see the separate [Nature](/interests/nature/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about nature and wildlife on this route

### Can I see giant tortoises on the itinerary?

Yes. The Santa Cruz Highlands excursion is specifically devoted to observing giant tortoises in their natural habitat. Where the animals are found and how they behave depends on conditions that day.

### Which islands are visited after Santa Cruz?

One of two options is provided: North Seymour with Bachas, or South Plaza with Carrion Point. The final choice is confirmed when booking.

### Is there wildlife watching in Uruguay and Chile?

There are no separate wildlife-watching excursions on the relevant days of this tour. Montevideo has a city sightseeing program, Santiago has a city tour, and the itinerary then stops in the Atacama region.

### Should I choose this trip solely for the Galápagos?

If your priority is several days of wildlife encounters and a choice of different islands, first compare the duration of more specialized Ecuador itineraries. Here the Galápagos are part of a major eight-country journey, and the time spent in the archipelago is limited by the overall schedule.

buttonLabel: "Learn more about journeys through Chile and Peru"
lead: >-
  Chile and Peru in one trip combine Pacific coast cities, Inca heritage and the high-altitude landscapes of the Andes. When choosing an itinerary, first check whether it travels directly between the neighboring countries or passes through Bolivia: Ada Tours offers programs with Lake Titicaca, Uyuni and Atacama between the Peruvian and Chilean sections. This affects the number of border crossings, overnight elevations, flights, documents, costs and the best season to travel.
---

## Chile and Peru: how a journey across the Andes really works

**The most important part of a Chile-and-Peru itinerary is the order of stops, not the number of countries in its title.** The two countries share a border, yet many of Ada Tours' more extensive routes connect them via Bolivia. On such a journey, you start in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), explore [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), travel up to [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), cross the Bolivian Altiplano, then enter Chile through the [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) region and finish in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

The “Chile + Peru” selection therefore includes itineraries in which Bolivia is a fully fledged third country. Our current trips are listed below; their number and composition update with the catalog: {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. If you want to visit exactly two countries, check each tour's itinerary separately. Traveling in the reverse order is also possible, but requires a different calculation of altitude changes and transfers.

### Three genuinely different ways to travel

| Route | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| Peru → Bolivia → Chile | Titicaca, Uyuni, Atacama |
| Chile → Bolivia → Peru | Atacama first, Machu Picchu closer to the end |
| Peru → Chile directly | A different route without stops in Bolivia |

The last row describes a geographically possible combination, **not a promise of an existing Ada Tours package**. Tacna–Arica is a reference point for a direct land border crossing; it does not replace the current tours traveling through Bolivia. If your main goals are [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the [Atacama Desert](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), reducing the number of intermediate overnight stops can make more sense than trying to include every available attraction.

## Which Ada Tours itineraries should you choose?

**[Peru, Bolivia and Chile in 14 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/)** connects Lima, Cusco, Puno, La Paz, Uyuni, Chile's Atacama region and Santiago in that order. An important advantage of this sequence is that altitude changes occur in stages, although acclimatization is still necessary. An optional visit to Easter Island is offered; treat it as a separate extension rather than an obligatory part of the 14 days.

**[VIP tour of Chile, Bolivia and Peru](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-vip/)** travels in the opposite direction: Santiago, Atacama, Uyuni, La Paz, Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima. It suits travelers who want to begin in Chile and devote the end of their journey to Peruvian history. The VIP designation places it in a separate selection; check the actual offer for the exact arrangements for guides, accommodation and transport.

**[Grand 33-day VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/)** adds the Peruvian Amazon, more stops in Chile, Easter Island and Patagonia to the three-country combination. It is a trip on a different scale in both time and logistics. It appeals to those who want to explore the countries in depth rather than cross the Andes in two weeks.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_velikij_tur_po_yuzhnoj_amerike,tour_source_vip_tur_v_peru,tour_south_america_luxury_33_days}}

If Brazil and Argentina also matter to you, consider the [18-day group itinerary through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). Its Chile-to-Peru section travels through Bolivia, so it appears in this catalog even though the full trip covers considerably more countries. The [multi-country travel](/multi-country/) section sets out the broader principles for choosing combinations.

## Borders and documents: why a third country changes the planning

For international travelers, **entry documents must be checked for every country they actually enter**, including transit that involves passport control. For example, a holder of an ordinary Russian international passport traveling Peru → Bolivia → Chile must check the entry rules of all three countries separately for the departure date. As of October 15, 2026, Peru's Ministry of Foreign Affairs publishes an official list of visa exemptions by nationality, while Chile's consular service publishes rules on prior visas and temporary stays. Bolivia requires its own check. Permission to enter Peru does not automatically cover Chile or Bolivia.

Planning should account for passport validity, blank pages, the ticket itinerary, proof of accommodation, permitted duration of stay and any onward or return ticket requirements. If the tour returns to Peru or Bolivia after Chile, check the rules for **re-entry**, rather than assuming that the conditions for a single crossing apply. The connecting airport outside these countries also matters: some transfers require entering the transit country.

The land journey from Peru's Puno to the Bolivian part of Lake Titicaca and La Paz is different from the high-altitude Bolivia–Chile border crossing near Atacama. Border-control time, weather and road conditions need separate allowances in the schedule. Avoid booking a nonrefundable international flight immediately after a long road transfer across a border.

Ada Tours helps arrange the sequence of countries, discuss document requirements for your particular nationality in advance and allow sufficient connection time. This is organizational assistance, **not a guarantee of obtaining a visa or being admitted at the border**.

## Altitude, climate and seasons: combining contrasting regions

[Lima](/peru/place/lima/) is on the coast, whereas [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) lies at approximately 3,350 m above sea level and Bolivia's [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) at about 3,650 m. Traveling to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and high-altitude lagoons involves further extended stretches across the Altiplano. Even a physically fit traveler can experience altitude sickness. Time-zone changes and long flights add fatigue, but **they do not replace acclimatization**.

Gentle walks and a lighter schedule are useful during the first days at altitude. Travelers with heart or lung disease, difficulty tolerating altitude or other significant medical conditions should discuss the itinerary with a doctor before buying. Choose insurance that covers the actual altitude reached, remote-area travel and planned activities. Medical evacuation provisions matter, not just the total coverage amount.

The climate also changes dramatically. Peru's Pacific coast, cool evenings in Cusco, cold and windy highlands and the dry Atacama all call for different clothing. In the Peruvian and Bolivian Andes, roughly May through September often brings drier weather; during the rainy season, mountain roads and visibility can be more challenging. Seasonality in Chile depends on the region: Santiago's weather and desert nighttime temperatures can differ even within the same month.

Layered clothing works well: lighter items for cities, warm layers for evenings and early mornings, sun protection, a rain jacket, sturdy walking shoes and a compact daypack. Check baggage allowances on domestic flights and rules for carrying equipment against the actual tickets, rather than assuming the limits of a long-haul flight apply.

## Money, connectivity and expenses along the route

Peru's main currency is the **Peruvian sol (PEN)**; Chile uses the **Chilean peso (CLP)**, and a visit to Bolivia adds the **boliviano (BOB)**. Carrying a reserve in US dollars alone will not solve every issue with small purchases, transport and payments at remote stops. Even where dollars are accepted, a seller's exchange rate may differ from a bank's.

Check in advance whether **your specific bank cards** work in each country and at all points on the itinerary. Cards issued by Russian banks require particular attention: international payment restrictions and acceptance of different payment networks cannot be determined from the logo on a card alone. Agree on a reserve of cash and legal ways to exchange it during the trip. ATMs may charge local fees and impose withdrawal limits; these need to be considered separately across three currency areas.

Easy-to-miss extra expenses include domestic airline baggage, excursions beyond the included program, meals outside the paid package, fees in individual parks and accommodation supplements. The services in the [14-day Peru, Bolivia and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) differ from those in the [12-day VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-vip/); compare the terms of each product, not merely the shared word “tour.”

## Machu Picchu, flights and time buffers

Tickets for [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) are sold for a **specific circuit and entry time**. Peru's Ministry of Culture is developing the Tu Boleto system; direct sales with payment confirmation were being introduced from September 2026. That means admission tickets and train or road transfers to the site need to be coordinated while choosing travel dates. A ticket for one circuit does not permit unrestricted access to every trail in the complex.

International and domestic flights may connect Lima, Cusco and Santiago, while the Bolivian portion can include road transfers. Throughout the itinerary, distinguish between flights, transfers and guided excursions; the word “transfer” in a day's description does not by itself specify the vehicle or duration. When connecting from an international to a domestic flight, find out whether you need to collect your baggage and check in again.

**A successful journey across the Andes leaves time to enjoy the actual places.** If the schedule is overloaded, remove one extra stop or add a night near the main attraction. Ada Tours can coordinate the sequence, transport and a more relaxed pace, especially on high-altitude stretches.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Chile and Peru

### Can Chile and Peru be combined without Bolivia?

Yes. The countries share a border and can be visited directly. However, Ada Tours' current selection includes itineraries through Bolivia with Uyuni and Titicaca. For a trip strictly limited to two countries, study each offer's complete country list: filtering for Chile and Peru does not exclude a third country.

### Should I start in Chile or Peru?

It depends on your priorities and the altitude profile. The [14-day Peru, Bolivia and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/) starts in Lima; the [VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-vip/) starts in Santiago. Compare not only price and duration, but also the elevation of your first overnight stops and the order of border crossings.

### How much time do Machu Picchu and Atacama require?

Consider the entire itinerary, including travel from Cusco to Machu Picchu and the journey to Atacama. Trying to fit both into a few days can mean spending much of your vacation in transit. Ada Tours offers complete 12- and 14-day itineraries with Bolivia between those destinations.

### Will Russian bank cards and US dollars work?

There is no universally positive answer. Check acceptance of your particular card with its bank, payment system and destination country. For Peru, Chile and Bolivia, it is sensible to plan for cash and exchange into local currencies; dollar bills cannot replace soles, pesos and bolivianos in every situation.

### What about visas for travelers who are Russian citizens?

Check Peru's and Chile's requirements for holders of ordinary Russian international passports, and Bolivia's rules if you travel through that country. Allow for possible repeat entries, transit countries and passport validity. The latest requirements should be verified against the actual travel date and route.

## Adventures in Chile and Peru: what is included and what must be booked separately

Combining [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/) appeals to travelers who want to see the arid [Atacama Desert](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), high mountain passes, Inca valleys and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) on one journey. These places are in the Andean region, but the ways of exploring them vary from a vehicle-supported excursion to a long off-road drive or a genuine hiking trek.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining Chile and Peru as principal countries with an adventure element. **The adventure itself may take place in a third country.** For example, intensive 4×4 days around high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni salt flat are in [Bolivia](/bolivia/). Likewise, reaching Machu Picchu by bus and train with a guide does not, by itself, mean hiking the Inca Trail.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama as the starting point for the mountain section

[San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) is a gateway to northern Chile's desert landscapes and trips toward the Bolivian border. The area has dry valleys, volcanic mountains, salt flats and substantial changes in elevation. Travelers should establish exactly which places are included and how the ascent is arranged.

On the [12-day Chile, Bolivia and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/), a sightseeing tour of Santiago is followed by a flight to Calama and a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama. This day is also intended for adjustment before the next stage. An evening stargazing excursion is listed as optional, so it should not be counted as an included service.

The travelers then cross the border for a two-day journey by 4×4 vehicles across the Bolivian Altiplano. The route includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), geyser fields, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Uyuni salt flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). **This section takes place in Bolivia, not in Chile's desert.** It involves long drives, cold conditions, intense sunshine and elevations exceeding 4,000 m in places.

An off-road expedition is different from a mountain ascent on foot. A jeep can reach remote lagoons and viewpoints, yet the altitude can be physically demanding even without lengthy hikes.

## Peru: cultural sightseeing or hiking in the Andes

In Peru, many combined journeys travel through [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), then on to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Climate, altitude and scenery change along this route. The difficulty, however, depends on the activities included.

Visits to Cusco, [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/), the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and Machu Picchu are primarily cultural and historical excursions with walking sections at the sites. A standard train-and-bus trip to Machu Picchu does not include a multi-day approach on the Inca Trail. Trekking requires a separate itinerary, an authorized route, appropriate permits and preparation.

On the [18-day tour through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), the Bolivian off-road section is followed by Titicaca, a group transfer from Puno to Cusco and a guided visit to Machu Picchu. It involves frequent changes in elevation and much time on the road, but the description does not present its Peruvian section as an expedition with daily strenuous hikes.

It helps to define your main goal before choosing: do you want to drive through a high-altitude desert, see an ancient city or complete a real mountain trek on foot? Each requires different days and equipment.

## Adventure itineraries worth comparing

| Tour | Main exertion and travel format |
|---|---|
| Chile, Bolivia, Peru — 12 days | Off-road section across the Altiplano |
| Five countries — 18 days | Many transfers, Uyuni, Titicaca |
| Peru, Bolivia, Chile — 14 days | Extended journey through the Andes |
| Grand VIP route — 33 days | Many different kinds of excursions |

**[Chile, Bolivia and Peru in 12 days](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/)** is the most direct option in this group if you want to travel from Chile's Atacama region through Bolivian salt flats to Peru's historical sites. The expedition-style portion is concentrated in two days of 4×4 driving. Be sure to compare the overnight altitude, guide languages on different sections and included excursions.

**[Five Latin American countries in 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/)** adds Brazil and Argentina, Iguazu Falls, cities and flights. The high-altitude section in Bolivia remains, but there is less time in each individual country. It suits a broad introductory journey rather than an in-depth trek in Atacama.

**[Peru, Bolivia and Chile in 14 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-peru-bolivia-chile-easter-island/)** links Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni, Atacama and Santiago. It covers the same geographical sequence in a different direction. Optional extensions should be considered separately from the required itinerary.

**[33-day VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/)** includes the Amazon, Machu Picchu, Bolivia, Atacama, Easter Island and Patagonia. It features expedition outings alongside more comfortable travel arrangements. One important detail: the visit to Vinicunca on this tour is scheduled by helicopter, so it must not be advertised as a hike up Rainbow Mountain.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_chile_bolivia_peru_group_12_days_2026,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_source_velikij_tur_po_yuzhnoj_amerike,tour_south_america_luxury_33_days}}

## Altitude and physical effort: why they are different

On a route through the Andes, you may walk very little and still feel exhausted. Cusco sits at around 3,350 m, La Paz above 3,500 m, and some road sections of the Bolivian Altiplano exceed 4,000 m. At those elevations, less oxygen is available and ascending too quickly increases the risk of altitude sickness.

**Fitness does not guarantee protection against altitude-related symptoms.** The sequence of overnight stays and the speed of ascent matter. Before traveling through high-altitude regions, discuss your health with a doctor. If symptoms develop during the trip, follow the instructions of trained accompanying staff and medical advice.

Layered clothing, sun protection and comfortable footwear for short walks on uneven ground are useful for Atacama and the high-altitude lagoons. A full mountain trek requires a different equipment list. Ask not only about the total trip length, but also the duration of daily walks and transfers and the elevation of overnight stops.

## Choosing a program and tickets without overloading the journey

Start by listing the days you are traveling for: Atacama, the high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni and Machu Picchu. Then check whether each attraction is actually included, which country it belongs to and how you get there. Mark free time and optional excursions separately: mentioning an activity in a city description does not make it an included service.

Machu Picchu has designated visitor circuits and limited-access tickets. Scenic walks and hiking routes around the archaeological complex vary. If you want to take a challenging trail independently or attempt a climb, arrange it while designing the trip rather than expecting to change an ordinary sightseeing ticket on arrival.

Compare [adventure tours in Chile](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/) and [adventure tours in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/). The [complete Chile and Peru selection](/multi-country/chile_peru/) shows trips regardless of theme. The [main adventure section](/interests/adventure/) offers further active travel options across Latin America.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Chile and Peru

### Which tour includes a jeep trip through high-altitude lagoons?

The [12-day Chile–Bolivia–Peru group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) includes two days in 4×4 vehicles through Bolivia's highlands, including the lagoons and Uyuni. Chile's Atacama Desert comes before this section, but the main off-road days take place across the border.

### Is the Inca Trail included in every Machu Picchu tour?

No. Visiting Machu Picchu by transport with a guided tour is different from multi-day trekking. If your aim is to hike the Inca Trail, choose a specific trekking itinerary and arrange permits in advance.

### Is a high-altitude tour suitable without mountaineering experience?

Some itineraries rely mainly on road transfers and guided excursions, so mountaineering experience is not listed as a requirement. However, the considerable altitude calls for a separate assessment of your health, ascent schedule and accommodation conditions.

### Can I visit only Chile and Peru, leaving out Bolivia?

Geographically, yes, but the ready-made adventure itineraries listed here include Bolivia as a fully fledged third country. In particular, Uyuni is in Bolivia. If you require a route through exactly two countries, its details need to be agreed separately.

lead: >-
  On Ada Tours' itinerary combining Peru and Chile, the true multi-day cruise takes place in the Peruvian Amazon aboard Aqua Nera. The journey then continues by train through the Andes, on an off-road route across Bolivia and on a major overland expedition through Chile as far as Easter Island and Patagonia. ## Cruises and expeditions through Peru and Chile: where the voyage takes place

The selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Currently this is the [33-day VIP itinerary through Peru, Bolivia and Chile](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/). Its geographical coverage extends beyond the two countries in the catalog title: travelers cross Bolivia after Peru before exploring several regions of Chile.

**The multi-day cruise takes place in Peru.** It is a voyage along Amazonian rivers aboard Aqua Nera, starting after a flight to Iquitos. The journey in Chile has a different character: the Atacama Desert, Easter Island, Patagonia, the Lake District and the Marble Caves. It would therefore be a mistake to choose this trip expecting an uninterrupted sea cruise between Peruvian and Chilean ports.

## Peru: the Amazon aboard Aqua Nera

After exploring Lima and taking a private flight over the Nazca Lines, the itinerary includes a yacht trip to the Ballestas Islands. A flight to [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/) follows, marking the start of the Aqua Nera cruise, which lasts **5 days and 4 nights**.

During the voyage, travelers experience the Amazon's river landscapes. The ship's program includes outings with experienced guides and opportunities to observe the rainforest, waterways and wildlife of the region. Each day's activities depend on actual navigation and the ship's operating conditions, so no specific animal encounter or unchanging order of expedition excursions can be promised in advance.

After the cruise, the plan calls for a flight from Iquitos to Cusco via Lima and a transfer to the Sacred Valley of the Incas. This is a different stage of the journey. Allow time for the flights and the transition from the river's humid heat to Peru's mountainous regions.

## The Andes: the expedition continues overland

The Peruvian section includes [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) with the Hiram Bingham train, followed by a journey on the Belmond Andean Explorer from Cusco toward Lake Titicaca. It is important to distinguish these experiences: the Belmond Andean Explorer is **an overnight train journey**, not a river or sea cruise. Lake Titicaca is visited on a separate part of the itinerary.

After entering Bolivia, the route heads for the Uyuni salt flat and the lagoons of the Altiplano. Modes of transport change throughout: plane, cruise vessel, train, car and boat. Some stretches offer comfortable relaxation; others involve early departures and considerable altitude. This combination of expedition formats is what distinguishes the 33-day journey.

## Chile: Atacama, Easter Island and Patagonian lakes

The Chilean section starts after the high-altitude Bolivian stage around [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Next are the El Tatio geysers, Valley of the Moon and night-sky observation, a flight to Santiago and then a journey to [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/). The program there centers on Rapa Nui sites, not on a multi-day sea voyage.

The next major natural region is Chilean Patagonia. The tour travels through Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine, then Puerto Varas and Chiloé Island. Visiting Chiloé involves a crossing of the Chacao Channel; the Puñihuil penguin colony is visited **only when the weather is suitable**.

Later, travelers take a boat excursion to the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) on General Carrera Lake. This is a local water excursion, not a reason to describe the entire Chilean section as an ocean cruise.

## What to compare before choosing the trip

| Travel format | Where it takes place |
|---|---|
| Aqua Nera cruise | Peruvian Amazon |
| Expedition jeeps | Bolivian Altiplano |
| Overnight train | Peru, route toward Titicaca |
| Short boat journeys | Peru and Chile |
| Overland route | Chilean Patagonia |

For the cruise, check boarding arrangements, the flight to Iquitos, baggage allowances and the order of landings and outings. For the high-altitude and Patagonian stages, consider altitude tolerance, roads, weather and the density of consecutive travel days. The tour lasts 33 days, so the comfort of the cruise itself should be considered alongside the entire subsequent journey.

Only one ready-made program is currently listed in this catalog. If a river cruise is your sole priority, start by examining the Aqua Nera section in Peru. If you want to combine sailing with the Andes and Patagonia, the [full 33-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) offers an extensive option with different kinds of transport. Compare the broader geography on the [Chile and Peru tours page](/multi-country/chile_peru/) and in the [cruises and expeditions section](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/).

## Frequently asked questions about cruises and expeditions in Peru and Chile

### Where does the Aqua Nera cruise begin and end?

On the current tour, the cruise starts after the flight to Iquitos and ends with a transfer to Iquitos airport. The cruise program is listed as 5 days and 4 nights; the ship's own schedule determines the precise sequence of river excursions.

### Is there a cruise along the Chilean coast?

This 33-day product does not include a multi-day cruise along Chile's coastline. Chile features overland journeys, short crossings and a boat excursion to the Marble Caves.

### Can I count on seeing penguins on Chiloé?

The visit to the Puñihuil area is expressly subject to favorable weather. Wildlife sightings and whether an outing is possible depend on conditions that day.

### Is the Belmond Andean Explorer part of the cruise?

No. It is an overnight railway journey, separate from the Amazon voyage aboard Aqua Nera. Both stages are included in the longer combined itinerary.

## Chilean and Peruvian culture on one journey: which heritage sites will you actually see?

A journey through [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/) can easily focus on history, but the countries have distinct cultural emphases. In Chile, Ada Tours itineraries explore [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), including Plaza de Armas, La Moneda Palace and its city districts. In Peru, travelers visit [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), landmarks of the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Together, these places help explain the development of Andean societies before the Spanish conquest and the later transformation of South American cities.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which Chile and Peru are principal countries and culture and history are significant parts of the itinerary. **The selection also contains trips through Bolivia, Argentina and Brazil.** A cultural theme applies to the journey as a whole and does not, by itself, confirm a separate historical monument or excursion in every country.

## How the historical stops in the two countries differ

**Santiago** introduces Chile's urban history through its central square, civic buildings, the capital's development and modern neighborhoods. The [12-day Chile–Bolivia–Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/) includes a Santiago sightseeing tour. The journey then continues to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and onward through Bolivia toward Cusco. The Chilean portion primarily introduces the capital and high-altitude landscapes; a separate excursion to Valparaíso is not included in this program.

**Valparaíso** reveals another side of Chilean history: port trade, a multicultural setting and neighborhoods built on steep hills. The port's historic quarter is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The [15-day Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) devotes a day to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). It is suitable if you want to experience more of Chile than its capital alone.

**Cusco and the Sacred Valley** lead into pre-Hispanic history. On the itinerary, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is linked to archaeological monuments and a mountainous landscape where the Incas built roads, terraces and settlements. UNESCO recognizes Machu Picchu for both cultural and natural heritage. Even if a tour includes a bus ride up to the complex, this does not mean it follows the famous Inca Trail on foot.

**Easter Island, or Rapa Nui**, is a distinct cultural chapter of Chile. The [33-day grand South America tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) includes Easter Island, Rano Kau, Orongo and moai sites. Such a route deserves separate comparison: the island flight and several days of exploration significantly affect the time budget. Rapa Nui is not automatically part of every Chile-and-Peru tour.

## Three genuinely different itineraries

| Program | Historical emphasis |
|---|---|
| Chile – Bolivia – Peru, 12 days | Santiago, Tiwanaku, Cusco |
| Four countries, 15 days | Valparaíso, Sacred Valley |
| Grand route, 33 days | Peru, Rapa Nui, southern Chile |

On the [12-day group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-group-12-days/), the Uyuni salt flat, La Paz and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) lie between the Chilean and Peruvian sections. This gives travelers a chance to see the monuments of the Tiwanaku civilization, which flourished before the height of the Inca Empire. The Bolivian stop adds a distinct historical period and requires time for travel at high altitude.

The [15-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) follows a different cultural thread: cities on the Atlantic and Pacific coasts, Valparaíso, then the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu. It is well suited to comparing city life and Andean heritage, although the number of flights and country changes leaves less time for detailed exploration of each monument.

The [33-day program](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) allows for a more extended immersion: historic Lima, several sites in Peru's Sacred Valley, then Chile's capital, Rapa Nui and other regions of Chile. It extends far beyond cultural history to nature and expedition activities. Do not choose it solely because it carries the “Culture and History” tag.

## Why the itinerary may pass through a third country

Chile and Peru share a border, but the listed journeys do not always cross directly between them. Many pass through Bolivia, which changes the experience. If the route includes [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), the historical scope extends beyond Inca heritage to another ancient Andean civilization. If only jeep drives to lagoons and salt flats are scheduled, the Bolivian section will mainly be about nature.

The Qhapaq Ñan, an ancient Inca road network linking territories in what are now Peru, Chile, Bolivia and other countries, demonstrates the shared history of several Andean nations. But **visiting cities in the former empire does not mean touring a specific protected section of this road**. That requires an explicitly named stop in the program.

When comparing trips, first check the day-by-day excursions and then the transport. For a history-focused journey, two substantive days in Cusco and the Sacred Valley will usually provide more than several brief stops spread across different cities.

## Altitude, tickets and time for sightseeing

Cusco is approximately 3,350 m above sea level, while Bolivia's La Paz and many parts of the Altiplano are even higher. Ascending rapidly from lowland cities calls for care. When planning cultural excursions, we can coordinate the order of stops and time to adjust; any health concerns related to the trip should be discussed with a doctor before departure.

At [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), the exact date, designated visitor circuit, named admission ticket and transport to the complex matter. Having Machu Picchu on a tour does not allow travelers to change their entry time or walking circuit at will. It is best to arrange these details in advance, especially when transfers and domestic flights are scheduled for the same days.

To select the cultural and historical elements independently of a broader journey, compare [culture and history tours in Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/) and [in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). For all destinations and country combinations, see the [general Culture and History catalog](/interests/culture-and-history/) and [Chile + Peru itineraries](/multi-country/chile_peru/).

## Frequently asked questions about the culture and history of Chile and Peru

### Which tour includes Valparaíso?

The [15-day journey through Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) sets aside a full day for Valparaíso and Viña del Mar. It may be absent from programs where the Chilean section is limited to Santiago and a flight to Calama.

### Can I visit Machu Picchu without a multi-day trek?

Yes. Ada Tours' current programs include visits to the complex using organized transport and guided sightseeing. Hiking the Inca Trail is a separate activity, and you need to look for it in the specific tour itinerary.

### Why is Bolivia included in a cultural selection?

Some tours covering Chile and Peru include Bolivia as a principal third country. [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) adds monuments from a pre-Inca civilization, while [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the lagoons belong mainly to the nature-focused portion of the journey.

### Should I choose the longest tour for its history?

Length alone guarantees nothing. Look at how many days are devoted to monuments, museums, historic neighborhoods and local traditions. A long itinerary may include several additional natural regions, while a shorter one spends more time on the cultural program itself.
